findings.title: tally.py and Audit/count.py report a module ok from its last good build's trace after its rebuild fails
findings.scenario: A module built cleanly once. Later only its imports, the lakefile pins or the toolchain change, not its own source; chunk 46 step 4's re-pin is the planned case. Its rebuild now fails. Chunk 46 recorded exactly this on PR #77: Seedelf.PolicyLinesAll failed on the new PlutusCoreBlaster, and LinesAllAnyMint failed through its import. Lake writes a module's .trace only when its build succeeds, and it never deletes the old one. So the failed module keeps its old trace: the old successful log, with an mtime still newer than its unchanged source. `python3 -I tally.py Seedelf` then lists it as ok and counts its old ✅. `python3 -I Audit/count.py` does the same, and so does Audit/run-all.sh's count.txt, the audit's last word on a run. The real result (FAILED) appears only in check.sh's console summary. A ✅ count or an audit verdict taken from these tools can include modules that no longer build. Downstream modules that can't build behind the failure keep their stale traces too.
findings.evidence:
- seedelf-verification/tally.py:59-68: `trace = os.path.join(root, ".lake", "build", "lib", "lean", rel + ".trace")` … `("built before its source changed", os.path.getmtime(trace) < os.path.getmtime(src))`. That is its only freshness test, and it compares against the module's own source alone.
- Its docstring (:11) says "Lake writes no trace for a failed build".
- seedelf-verification/Audit/count.py:79-82: `if not os.path.exists(trace): return "NO TRACE", "never built, or its build failed: see check.sh's output"` and `if os.path.getmtime(trace) < os.path.getmtime(src): return "STALE"`. Its docstring (:15) makes the same assumption: a failed build shows as NO TRACE.
- Lake v4.24.0 (the pinned toolchain), ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.24.0/src/lean/lake/Lake/Build/Common.lean:224-243: buildAction's doc says the log "[is] saved to `traceFile`, if the build completes without a fatal error". The code is `let outputs ← build -- fatal errors will abort here` and then `writeBuildTrace traceFile …`. Nothing removes the old file.
- Module.lean:632: `Module.buildLean … := buildAction depTrace mod.traceFile do … compileLeanModule …`. Actions.lean's compileLeanModule creates directories and runs lean, and removes no output.
- seedelf-verification/Audit/run-all.sh:29: `./check.sh "$f" 2>&1 | tee "Audit/logs/$f.log"` drops check.sh's exit status, and :33 runs count.py last.
- Read-only check of the copied .lake, with my scratch script v3_trace_ages.py: 140 of 655 traced modules have a trace older than a direct import's trace. All 140 are Audit modules (built 2026-11-03; the proofs were rebuilt on 11-04). count.py would judge them only against their own sources. No proof module is in that state today.
- A verifier can show the mechanism in a two-module scratch Lake package outside seedelf-verification: build it, break the import, rebuild (it fails), then apply tally.py's freshness rule to the importer's .trace.
findings.fix: Make a failed build show as one. Option (a): check.sh removes a listed module's .trace when its build ends non-zero, so the readers see NO TRACE, as both docstrings already assume. Option (b): tally.py and count.py, two copies of the same freshness rule, also flag a trace older than any imported module's trace in the package (transitively), or older than lakefile.lean, lake-manifest.json or lean-toolchain. Option (c): check.sh writes each run's verdict per module, and both readers refuse a module whose last verdict wasn't ok.
findings.known_check: Searched seedelf-verification/Audit/review/findings.md (script-hex-not-lake-inputs, checksh-cannot-tell-replay, lovejoin-traces-predate-edits, policyburn-policymint-no-trace, z3-binary-unpinned), docs/backlog.md, docs/archive/plans/ and the verification READMEs for tally, count.py, "stale trace", "failed build", "no trace", depHash and "older than". None records a successful trace surviving a failed rebuild. The two tools' docstrings assume the opposite. Chunk 49 step 1 is about .hex inputs only.

findings.title: CI skips the proven-bytes test on a PR that changes only the proven .hex files it reads
findings.scenario: A PR touches only seedelf-verification/, for example to move the proofs onto new Lovejoin bytes: it re-extracts Lovejoin/Template/Scripts/*.hex with the extract's pinned hashes updated, or edits a .hex by hand. Web Wallet's path filter covers only seedelf-platform/ (minus Markdown and media/), the workflow file and wasm/README.md. So `changes` sets platform=false, the rust job (`cargo test --workspace --locked`) is skipped, and `Web Wallet required` passes with every job skipped. lovejoin_proven_bytes_test would fail on that PR, but it never runs, so the PR merges green. The wallet keeps launching and verifying pools from templates.rs's old Set::V2 bytes, while the proofs (after a rebuild) are about other bytes. CLAIMS.md still says the live pool runs exactly the proven templates, citing that test. The break shows only in main's post-merge run, which no one waits on, or on the next platform PR.
findings.since: 96f9b40d (web-wallet/1.8.1), when the test began reading seedelf-verification/; the filter is from 9e5520f9
findings.evidence:
- .github/workflows/web-wallet.yml:67: `covered='/^\.github\/workflows\/web-wallet\.yml$/ || /^seedelf-platform\/seedelf-web-wallet\/wasm\/README\.md$/ || (/^seedelf-platform\// && !/\.md$/ && !/^seedelf-platform\/seedelf-web-wallet\/media\//) …'`.
- The rust job (:74-109) runs only `if: needs.changes.outputs.platform == 'true'`.
- `required` (:297-299) is green when every job was skipped (docs/development.md:13).
- The workflow's own rule (:35-38) adds a file outside the filter only for Markdown: "except wasm/README.md (readme_test.rs reads its export table). A test that comes to read another .md file names it here too."
- seedelf-platform/seedelf-web-wallet/wasm/tests/lovejoin_proven_bytes_test.rs:15-22 `include_str!`s four files outside seedelf-platform/: seedelf-verification/Lovejoin/Template/Scripts/{mix_logic,mix_box,one_shot_mint}.hex and Lovejoin/Scripts/reference_holder.hex. Its header (:1-5) says: "Edit either, and this fails."
- seedelf-verification/CLAIMS.md:23 and README.md:177 present this test as the check that mainnet's v2 pool (fcb3f5ec…) runs the proven templates.
- A grep of tests that read outside seedelf-platform/ finds only this one; the extension's fixtures read seedelf-crypto vectors inside it.
- main's push run sets platform=true (:60-62) and would fail after the merge (:10-12: "No one waits on that run").
- The extract scripts' own hash pins (extract-lovejoin-v2.sh:70-101) refuse unpinned bytes, so the gap needs a pin change or a hand edit.
findings.fix: Option (a): add the .hex paths the test reads to `covered`, either the four files or `^seedelf-verification\/.*\.hex$`, and widen the rule's comment from .md files to any file outside seedelf-platform/ that a test reads. Option (b), to keep verification PRs fast: a small job that runs only `cargo test -p seedelf-wasm --test lovejoin_proven_bytes_test` when seedelf-verification/**/*.hex changes, listed in `required`'s needs. Today this test is the only member of the class.
findings.owner_why: It changes what CI runs, and how long it takes, for verification-only PRs (the owner's 'CI speed matters' rule): adding these paths runs the whole suite, while a small dedicated job doesn't.
findings.known_check: Searched docs/backlog.md, docs/archive/plans/, docs/development.md, seedelf-verification/*.md and Audit/review/findings.md for proven_bytes, "proven bytes", "path filter" and seedelf-verification together with CI. development.md:13 documents the filter's scope. v2-launch-not-tied-to-proved-templates was closed by adding this test. Nothing notes that CI skips it on the PRs that change one of its two sides.

findings.title: tally.py's docstring says check.sh's ok can't tell Valid from Undetermined, but since #372 check.sh can
findings.scenario: A contributor deciding which verdict to trust reads tally.py's docstring. It says check.sh's `ok` can't tell Valid from Undetermined. Since 2e6a4b51 (#372), check.sh reports such a module as UNDETERM and fails the run. The reader may distrust check.sh's summary, or think tally.py is needed to catch an Undetermined result, when what tally.py actually adds is per-source counts and the `sorry` check.
findings.since: 2e6a4b51 made the sentence false; it was written in a04ca256
findings.evidence:
- seedelf-verification/tally.py:10-11: "check.sh's `ok` can't tell Valid from Undetermined, since Blaster logs Undetermined as a warning only; this can."
- check.sh:217-218: `undet=$(grep -cE '^warning: .*Undetermined' "$outf")` and `[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ "$undet" -gt 0 ] && rc=undetermined`; :225 prints UNDETERM.
- Audit/count.py:13-14 was updated in the same commit (2e6a4b51) to say "check.sh reports such a module as UNDETERM, not ok". `git log` shows tally.py untouched since a04ca256.
findings.fix: Reword the docstring to say what tally.py adds over check.sh: it holds each module's ✅ count against its source, flags `sorry`, and reads the trace rather than the console. Fold this into v3#1's fix.
findings.known_check: Grepped the repository's Markdown for tally: only chunk 51's plan and lanes name it. Nothing records this sentence.

guards.stops: verify_pool, through templates::derive_for (templates.rs:179), refuses a pool whose datum's mix_logic isn't one of the bundled template sets applied to its seed's policy. No box goes to a mix_box that the bundled templates, V2's being the proven ones, don't derive.

Pins templates.rs's Set::V2 bytes and apply() to mainnet's live v2 pool, hash for hash: seed 6db8a313…#3, P fcb3f5ec…, L a6a85074…, M dd94113c…. A change to the bundled bytes or to how parameters are applied would derive a different pool for the same seed. Line 30 pins the bundled bytes to the proven .hex.
guards.test: itself (CI doesn't run it on a seedelf-verification-only PR: v3#2)

guards.stops: templates_are_frozen and v2_templates_are_frozen (:275) pin every bundled template's unapplied hash and both commits, so an edit to templates.rs can't move a set's derived pools.

A claim guard, not a money guard. Each extract writes a .hex only when its hash equals the pinned value: extract.sh:34-37 for Seedelf against constants' hashes, extract-lovejoin.sh:46-58 for the classic pool against Protocol::of and references.rs's outputs, and this one for v2's templates, the test launch, the classic mix_box and the retired 5 ₳ pool's policy and fee.
guards.test: none found (the scripts are run by hand)

checked_ok: The Seedelf scripts are the deployed bytes. Seedelf/Scripts/{wallet,seedelf,always_false}.hex equal 5b82530's contracts/*_contract.plutus, one CBOR layer, byte for byte (PlutusScriptV3). Their hashes 94bca9c0…, 84967d91… and 6777ba4d… equal constants.rs's wallet_contract_hash and seedelf_policy_id, and the always_false address of the reference outputs.

wallet.hex and seedelf.hex each sit, as [3, bytes] script refs, inside references.rs's PREPROD_ and MAINNET_ WALLET and SEEDELF reference outputs. Their sizes, 629 and 519, equal constants.rs's wallet_contract_size and seedelf_contract_size.

Lovejoin/Template/Scripts/{mix_logic,mix_box,one_shot_mint,fee_contract}.hex equal templates.rs's MIX_LOGIC_V2, MIX_BOX, ONE_SHOT_MINT and FEE_CONTRACT byte for byte: 7fb45b75…, 2365a62d…, 6878ed6f…, 3698bbfd…, with lengths 3439, 594, 995 and 2251 as the doc comments say. Lovejoin/Scripts/reference_holder.hex equals templates.rs's REFERENCE_HOLDER (288fea77…).

Lovejoin/Scripts/*.hex (the classic pool) equal Lovejoin c1239fb's artifacts/mainnet/*.plutus. Their hashes match Protocol::of's mainnet values and the reference datum. mix_box and mix_logic sit inside references.rs's LOVEJOIN_MAINNET_MIX_BOX and MIX_LOGIC.
Lovejoin/V2/Scripts/mix_logic.hex hashes to 60294352…, the test launch the extract pins.

The wasm test's live-pool values (seed 6db8a313…#3, P fcb3f5ec…, L a6a85074…, M dd94113c…) equal lovejoin-pools.json's mainnet v2 pool. Its datum names the same M and L, and its reference scripts are 629 and 3487 bytes, a V2 mix_logic's length.

The kernel theorems apply parameters as the wallet does. toTerm x = Const (Data (toData x)), ByteString to B, Integer to I. The order is (P, "lovejoin") for mix_logic, (L) for mix_box and (seed tx, index, reference-holder hash) for one_shot_mint, matching templates.rs's apply() and NFT_NAME.
All nine gen-*.py, run in a scratch copy, reproduce the 247 committed files they write, byte for byte. gen-lovejoin-mix.py read its KATs from Lovejoin 29573c5's mix_kat.test.ak for this run.

The generators' step limits can't make a theorem vacuous. Every generated theorem asserts a positive outcome within the limit (isUnsuccessful = Error, isSuccessful, returnsUnit), and the Signers and Slice families also prove returns-unit-or-error.

Every module CLAIMS.md cites is in a standard check.sh family (seedelf-every, lovejoin-every, lovejoin-any-tx) and carries a #guard_msgs guard holding its axioms to Lean's three. Only the known LogicOwnerPrefix and LogicOwnerParserReach and the aggregators are in no family. lovejoin-every is 51 imports plus 25 of its own (76), and seedelf-every is 28, as chunk 46 counted.

The pins in lakefile.lean and Slice/lakefile.lean equal lake-manifest.json's revs, and the fetched packages in .lake are at those revs with no local changes.
- The dependencies' own requires (CardanoLedgerApi's PlutusCore@main and Blaster@beta, PlutusCore's Blaster@bc03bb4) yield to the root's pins.
- Slice's PlutusCoreBlaster pin (96261cc) differs from 68c5399 only in the opaque slice alias, one file, so both packages decode the same bytes with the same flat decoder.
Seedelf/, Lovejoin/ and Slice/ hold no sorry, admit, native_decide or axiom outside comments.
Every proof module's trace in the copied .lake is at least as new as each of its imports' traces.
Every proved script is Plutus V3: the envelopes, the reference outputs' language tag and Lovejoin's aiken.toml.
extract-lovejoin-v2.sh's cross-checks agree with the wallet's lovejoin-pools.json: the retired 5 ₳ pool's seed d4c72bc2…#0, policy dc6abe3b… and fee contract 20aae476…, and the classic L for mix_box.

The Signers' bound of 125 holds. Each signatory needs a 30-byte key hash and a 101-byte witness, and 16,384 / 131 = 125. The ledger decodes the required signers as a set, so the TxInfo never carries duplicates beyond it.
notes:
Stale provenance comments, the class r2-docs#13 left as is (editing a Scripts module rebuilds every module that imports it):
- Lovejoin/V2/Scripts.lean says the bytes come from the local-only ../../lovejoin-v2 clone at 5cc3631. The extract now builds Lovejoin main at 29573c5, and the hash is the same.
- Slice/Slice/Scripts.lean says "local-only `local/opaque-slice`". Slice/lakefile.lean fetches the fork's opaque-slice (96261cc) from GitHub.
- extract-lovejoin-v2.sh's header calls 8131b1d "the templates seedelf-core pins", but core pins both sets.
- seedelf-core's Protocol::of credits the classic artifacts to Lovejoin cb5a5a3, where extract-lovejoin.sh reads them at c1239fb; the bytes are equal.
extract-sh-own-pins-only (info, known): my read-only comparison shows every Seedelf .hex inside references.rs's on-chain reference outputs, so nothing needs fixing today.
gen-lovejoin-mix.py reads its KATs from the local-only ../../lovejoin-v2 clone (5cc3631, which still exists). With 29573c5's mix_kat.test.ak in its place, the generated modules are identical.

count.py never flags a `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning; it sees sorryAx only in #print axioms output, and Audit/Checks/PrintAxioms covers only the 313 scenario theorems of 2026-11-03. tally.py does flag sorry. So for the later Blaster families (AnyTx, Signers), the README's "read its output" and tally.py are the only sorry checks. That is documented. The kernel claims are guarded.
tally.py resolves its source paths against the current directory. Run from outside seedelf-verification/, it prints "0 modules … 0 not ok". count.py anchors on its own path.

In the copied .lake, 140 Audit modules' traces are older than an import's trace: the audit ran on 2026-11-03, and the proofs were rebuilt on 11-04. Wherever their sources predate those traces, count.py still reads them as ok. That fits Audit/README's "as they stood on 2026-11-03", but it is the same blind spot as v3#1.

Minor script hygiene, no harm found:
- extract-lovejoin-v2.sh leaves its mktemp folder behind when aiken build or apply fails, since it exits before the rm.
- check.sh silently drops any argument after a family name (`./check.sh lovejoin-every X` builds the family).
- Audit/run-all.sh's tee hides check.sh's exit status.

Lovejoin 29573c5 tracks contracts/plutus.opt.json, built with Aiken v1.1.21, whose hashes (mix_logic 8c626e11…) differ from the deployed ones. Neither the wallet nor the proofs read it. A reader matching bytes against it would find a false mismatch.
